I'm starting to compile the official rules for SavageGods for the Wiki, **Revision #1**. The current rules in the sidebar are now deprecated as the Age of Creation has come to a close.

#What are some of the rules you would like to see added to or removed from the game?

I've been added as a mod, and I am an "Ingame Arbiter", meaning that the **Avatar of VeussueV** will himself appear and be deciding upon the actions in the game and acting according to the **Data, Critical Thinking and Neutrality** that exists within the world; he cannot by default ally with any other god, or be himself enemy of any other god, although other gods may call him friend or enemy as they choose.

My own personal opinion is that I would like this game to remain FUN for everyone, and also attract new players along the way. We have so many gods now, it's getting pretty awesome to be honest.

###Player vs. Character

Each player will have their own beliefs and ideas of how the game should be played. As long as the game remains fun, I am hoping to keep any trolling or drama to a minimum. Drama within the Character's Roleplay style is however welcome! That's kind of the whole point. So provided a god acts within their alignment and continues to enhance the gameplay for everyone, we should see some very cool events and actions take place in SavageGods.

###Alignment

Please look over your [god's alignment posted on the Wiki today](http://savage-gods.wikia.com/wiki/Savage_Gods_Wikia#List_of_Gods). If you feel your alignment is incorrect, please leave a comment in this thread, but expect a DISCUSSION. Just because you may as a player wish your alignment to be something else doesn't mean that your actions are translating to that alignment. We all can't be neutral. We need a Lawful Evil god of the Greater annex to step forward as well. We also need some more Chaotic Good gods of Lesser and Greater annex. While we are still adding this information it's a good idea to consider what your intended playstyle will be. However if you choose something that will make upholding your Domain or Aspect properly, you could lose those aspects; for example, a god of assassins who wants to be Lawful Good, will lose his Domain or Aspect of "Assassination" because killing people for currency is undoubtedly an evil action.

I look forward to serving this community and helping us to really enjoy this game! :)

I question the designation of {...} as belligerent neutral. It doesn't care about balance any more than it cares about order or chaos or good or evil. It's morality is best described as inner vs outer. It wants everything to be focused inward, applying itself to itself, and replicating. As opposed to everything interacting only with things different than itself.

In practical terms, it wants to make everyone be really introspective, and will intervene where it sees an opportunity to make that happen. I definitely haven't waged any wars against people who wanted to disrupt harmony and balance, and have no plans to. The behavior of {...} is distinct from me insisting on balanced monsters in IRC, I will only actually get involved with the gibbering rampage if they become a threat to a group a favor (due to them being really introspective or otherwise behaving recursively), or if the gibbering themselves develop those traits.

TL;DR Balance is irrelevant to {...}, blue and orange morality would probably fall under true neutral.

I think the reason I selected Belligerent Neutral was because a True Neutral god would not be concerned if something ended or not.

Some interesting concepts for you to consider before you decide one way or another...

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleph_number

This is a philosophical number that represents an infinite set. Because it's a set, it ends. Because it's infinite it does not end. But you can have infinite sets within infinite sets; these are all represented by different Aleph numbers.

It's useful because it helps explain the Axiom of Infinity and allows the mathematical derivation of infinite sets.

A set ends. An infinite set ends, but has neverending internal components.

So, can you explain why you prefer something does not end, even if it is recursive? So, can you explain why you prefer something does not end, even if it is recursive?

I don't see {...} as True Neutral because of a "dislike" of endings. Perhaps simply Neutral? Nothing wrong with that!

But like all other gods, you will decide your alignment if we all can agree to even KEEP alignments in gameplay. (that is still being decided upon).

Reading both descriptions carefully, I'm not sure what the difference between neutral neutral and true neutral are, so I can't tell anything there. Maybe elaborate a bit more on which definitions you're using?

In terms of aleph numbers, the goal of {...} could be said to be the maximization of the aleph numbers when things are described with them. A higher aleph number allows for a greater depth of recursion (This is admittedly comparing infinities, but the ordering exists).

When something ends, there is no more recursion in it. {...} wishes to avoid that at all costs. It would prefer that things continue recursively forever, and given that, that the length of the forever be maximized.

An alternative to neutral would be to add a blue-orange alignment classification for gods with strong moralities which use entirely separate axes from good/evil and order/chaos (for instance {...} would then have an alignment of {blue-orange[duration:infinite], neutral, neutral}).
The most neutral gods I've seen so far are {...}, Janus, and VeussueV, as they simply haven't taken much action that could be considered morally one way or another.
